newsitem.title: UK: Premier Farnell says has base for growth.
newsitem.headline: Premier Farnell says has base for growth.

text.p: Electronic components distributor Premier Farnell said it was happy with its current company structure after it sold off Farnell Electronic Services in January.
"All of the divisions we have got now are high margin divisions. We now have a solid business for the future," said chief executive Howard Poulson said in an interview.
"What we have to do is drive that extra element of growth through our business," he added.
As distribution markets are showing no signs of picking up as yet, growth should come from efficiency measures and marketing initiatives, Poulson said.

One such initiative is the recent introduction of the Farnell product range in the U.S. With the range so far only available in a third of all branches, Poulton said there was good scope for further growth this year as it is being launched in other outlets.
In the U.K., Premier Farnell is seeking to boost sales through greater product availability and the introduction of a new industrial catalogue.
The company earlier reported that pre-tax profit before exceptional items rose 82 percent to 137.4 million stg.
The rise was held back by the current pound strength. Poulton said that every one cent increase in the dollar-pound exchange rate would reduce profit before tax by about one million dollars.
The pound's strength hit profits only because of currency translation, but did not hurt underlying business, Poulton said.
"The pound does not actually affect our trading in the U.S. market or any other market," Poulton said.
